name: Serial Port

claims.claim_text: A serial link needs a common ground between the two ends as well as the data lines; without a shared ground reference the receive and transmit pairs will not communicate at all.
claims.quote_verbatim: RX and TX won't transmit if there's no ground linking them
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jason Kridner and Robert Nelson

claims.claim_text: Reversed transmit and receive lines is the other standard first-connection fault, and it is common enough that a board can end up with the pair swapped twice and therefore working by accident.
claims.quote_verbatim: I actually swapped RX and TX twice on the board by accident
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jason Kridner and Robert Nelson

claims.claim_text: Serial access under Linux is architecture-independent: an application written as ordinary C against the operating system's serial interface can be rebuilt unchanged for a different processor family and behave the same way.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's just generic C for talking to a serial port in Linux
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jason Kridner and Robert Nelson

claims.claim_text: A point-to-point network gadget over USB cannot configure itself because the device has no way to detect which host operating system it is attached to, leaving per-platform setup that every user has to perform by hand.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's a little bit of setup that everyone has to do based on their systems
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jason Kridner and Robert Nelson

claims.claim_text: A development board that presents two serial ports, one for data and one for control, broke host-side detection because the tooling could not tell which was which.
claims.quote_verbatim: it doesn't detect the serial ports properly because it generates two serial ports
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The working out-of-box path for that kit was a browser talking to the board's serial port, with no need to install the vendor's full development environment, but nothing in the packaging said so and the source-only download implied the opposite.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a serial port. You don't have to install the Code Composer and all that
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth was conceived as a wireless replacement for a serial cable, which is why classic Bluetooth carries good support for presenting itself as a serial port to the host.
claims.quote_verbatim: Bluetooth was originally, I believe, designed to be a serial port replacement
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth Low Energy dropped that capability: it carries no serial port profile, so anyone wanting a transparent byte pipe over BLE has to improvise one.
claims.quote_verbatim: Bluetooth LE does not support serial ports over Bluetooth, for example. You know, you've got to cludge it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Low Energy is not a lighter version of classic Bluetooth but a different and considerably more rigid protocol, which catches out designers who assume feature parity.
claims.quote_verbatim: Bluetooth LE is much harder and much more inflexible, much less flexible than normal Bluetooth
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Automatic reset for programming came from soldering a capacitor between two pins so that the host's serial handshake line resets the board, removing the need to press a button at the right instant.
claims.quote_verbatim: if I solder a capacitor between these two pins, the serial port is resetting the board for me
claims.speaker: Massimo Banzi
claims.episode_title: Arduino's Invisible Touch with Massimo Banzi

claims.claim_text: The mechanism is edge conversion: the host asserts the data terminal ready line as the port opens, and the series capacitor turns that transition into a reset pulse rather than a level.
claims.quote_verbatim: the serial port moves this DTR right at the moment. And if you put a capacitor there, you generate a reset pin
claims.speaker: Massimo Banzi
claims.episode_title: Arduino's Invisible Touch with Massimo Banzi

claims.claim_text: That design came out of a teaching session where students could not get the manual reset timing right, so the fix was prompted by watching beginners fail rather than by a specification.
claims.quote_verbatim: someone there was having a lot of trouble pressing the buttons
claims.speaker: Massimo Banzi
claims.episode_title: Arduino's Invisible Touch with Massimo Banzi

claims.claim_text: The BASIC Stamp needed no separate programmer because the bootloader was already in the part, so a plain serial connection was enough to load a program, which is the same pattern later beginner boards used.
claims.quote_verbatim: it had the bootloader in there actually pre-programmed in and you can hook it up to a serial port
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Implementing the USB device inside the programmable fabric removed the external interface chip from the bill of materials, with the board enumerating on the host as an ordinary serial port.
claims.quote_verbatim: that USB connection, that USB device is implemented on the FPGA fabric itself
claims.speaker: Luke Valenty

claims.claim_text: That works because the part supports several configuration images in its flash with a primitive that selects which one to load next, so the USB personality can be the default boot and the application image loaded afterwards.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can have multiple configuration images
claims.speaker: Luke Valenty

claims.claim_text: A benchtop pick-and-place presents to the host as a COM port and runs 3D printer firmware, so it is effectively a printer with more axes and no hot end, which is why existing host software can drive it.
claims.quote_verbatim: it enumerates like a comp port on your computer
claims.speaker: Stephen Hawes
claims.episode_title: A Benchtop Pick and Place with Stephen Hawes

claims.claim_text: One USB connection can expose several independent serial ports at once, with one of them wired straight through to the board's own asynchronous lines so an attached module can be reached directly.
claims.quote_verbatim: we keep adding serial ports, but right now it's three serial ports
claims.speaker: Kevin Cappuccio
claims.episode_title: A Jumperless Breadboard with Kevin Cappuccio

claims.claim_text: Keeping the command format human-readable rather than binary let other people drive the instrument from whatever tool they already had, including a spreadsheet sending paths over its serial interface.
claims.quote_verbatim: I like it being like just human readable
claims.speaker: Kevin Cappuccio
claims.episode_title: A Jumperless Breadboard with Kevin Cappuccio

claims.claim_text: The transition away from native ports ran through plug-and-play converter modules and then single-chip USB-to-serial parts, which is the wave that made the dedicated converter vendors.
claims.quote_verbatim: on the backs of that FTDI emerges
claims.speaker: Matt Berggren

claims.claim_text: Legacy point-of-sale installations were built entirely on serial links running to a back office perhaps twenty metres away, which brought signal amplification and attenuation problems that the later USB world simply did not have.
claims.quote_verbatim: The back office might be, uh, you know, 20 meters away
claims.speaker: Matt Berggren

claims.claim_text: Embedded tooling still centres on Windows even as cross-platform support improves, while the Unix-side habit is to attach a terminal program straight to the port device.
claims.quote_verbatim: use Screen, you know, and you just like access the serial port directly
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The standing tradeoff with the Unix approach is capability against required expertise, summed up in the old saying that you can do anything but you have to be an expert to do it.
claims.quote_verbatim: with Unix you can do anything. But to do anything you have to be an expert
claims.speaker: Jack Ganssle

claims.claim_text: The most frequent cause of a serial link that will not talk is simply the wrong port selected on the host, particularly on a machine with several enumerated devices.
claims.quote_verbatim: the thing I find that's mostly wrong is I've chosen the wrong port
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The way to separate a host problem from a device problem is to put an instrument on the physical pins and see whether anything is being transmitted at all before debugging software.
claims.quote_verbatim: stick a scope or something else external on there just to see if it's pumping anything out
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Silicon errata can take out a peripheral completely, including entire serial ports that do not function and pins that are not where the datasheet says, with vendors sometimes supplying an unexplained instruction sequence as the workaround.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've had entire serial ports not working. I've had, uh, you know, pins swapped on the chip
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A low-baud-rate serial port can be kept running at around one microamp of current and move its data by direct memory access while the processor stays in a deep low-power state, so a link does not have to force the part awake.
claims.quote_verbatim: we have a low board rate serial port that can actually be active in a one microamp current consumption and move data via DMA
claims.speaker: Oyvind Janbu
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Øyvind Janbu - Feracious Fabless Facilitator

claims.claim_text: A measurement system consolidating a rack of instruments was built on a processor rather than a microcontroller because it needed deterministic timing while servicing several serial ports and incoming interrupts at once.
claims.quote_verbatim: needed all these multiple serial ports and there was interrupts coming in
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Needing six serial ports for six motor drives forced an awkward architecture of one master microcontroller feeding two slaves, which is exactly the situation a multi-drop bus removes.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've got one master Arduino. And then that sends serial to two slave Arduinos. And that's because I need six serial ports
claims.speaker: James Bruton

claims.claim_text: Industrial backplane computers solved the same problem with plug-in cards carrying eight serial ports each, alongside digital and relay input-output cards.
claims.quote_verbatim: you could get, you know, eight port RS two 32s if you need a bunch of serial ports
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Most handheld multimeters cannot be updated in the field at all, and those that can generally require a serial interface, which is why a memory-card update path is unusual.
claims.quote_verbatim: Most of them are like through the serial port, you know, you got to have the serial port interface and do it that way
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Reusing a familiar connector for a non-standard signal set requires explicit labelling on the product, because users will otherwise plug in equipment expecting the connector's usual function.
claims.quote_verbatim: then you have to be super explicit in like, this is not a serial port
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: For low-frequency interconnect between boards inside a rack, a board-mounted D connector that simply slides together is the pragmatic choice when the build quantity does not justify a custom cable.
claims.quote_verbatim: if it's not high frequency stuff, you might just use like a PCB mount D connector
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Describing a hardware debugger as a serial port into the processor misleads anyone whose background is beginner boards, because in that world the term means text going back and forth rather than register-level control.
claims.quote_verbatim: serial port, especially from the Arduino land means text back and forth
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: The actual low-level debug loop is a hardware probe on the processor's debug port with a debugger server, loading, resetting and running the image, plus a logic analyser on the flash bus to confirm the code is doing what was intended.
claims.quote_verbatim: I have on my desk, uh, J link connected to the SWD port that's on a Metro
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: For a sensitive measurement a lithium-ion cell is a genuinely low-noise supply compared with mains equipment, but choosing it means the instrument cannot stay tethered, so results leave over a wireless link that appears as a serial port on the host.
claims.quote_verbatim: another really low noise power source is a lithium ion battery
claims.speaker: Jean Rintoul

claims.claim_text: A module that merely streams measurements out as a serial port invites the question of whether it could serve a web interface instead, and the limit is usually the module's own capability rather than the idea.
claims.quote_verbatim: it just sort of like acts as a serial port, and it's just like spewing out data
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Older vehicle buses are best understood as a serial port with a fixed frame format: an oscilloscope shows the transitions but the encoding has to be known before the data means anything.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can kind of think of it like a serial port where it's a set type of, uh, communications bus
claims.speaker: Collin Kidder
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Earl Sharpe and Collin Kidder

claims.claim_text: On the Osborne 1 the general-purpose serial port ran only at 1200 and 300 baud because those were the only rates derivable from the existing video counter chain, a rate limit chosen for cost reduction rather than protocol reasons.
claims.quote_verbatim: you could only do 1200 and 300 ports. Because those were frequencies I could get from within the video count chain
claims.speaker: Lee Felsenstein
claims.episode_title: Lee Felsenstein: The Computer Revolution & Counterculture

claims.claim_text: The same connector was made to serve both the instrumentation bus the customer wanted and a general-purpose parallel port, with software rather than extra hardware doing the work.
claims.quote_verbatim: the port could be multipurpose as well as 488
claims.speaker: Lee Felsenstein
claims.episode_title: Lee Felsenstein: The Computer Revolution & Counterculture

claims.claim_text: Instrument control software has long been thin: decades of production test tooling amounted to sending bytes in and out of a serial port to configure equipment, which is why the host language mattered less than turnaround speed.
claims.quote_verbatim: it was mostly just sending stuff in and out of a serial port to like set something up or configure it
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Mike Harrison - X-ray Examining Xenogogue

claims.claim_text: A hardware reverse-engineering exercise models the real toolkit as a voltage probe, a pulse generator, register access over a debug interface and a serial port for reading and writing data.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have a serial port where you can read and write serial data
claims.speaker: Zach Barth
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Zach Barth of Zachtronics

claims.claim_text: Driver installation and identifying the right port are the single largest source of beginner support requests, so a board that mounts as a storage device instead removes an entire category of failure before it happens.
claims.quote_verbatim: software questions like instillation and comports are like number one questions you get
claims.speaker: Ken Burns

claims.claim_text: Making a board programmable over a plain serial connection, with no dedicated programmer in the way, was a deliberate route to lowering the barrier for people who only wanted to build something.
claims.quote_verbatim: You just hooked it up to a serial port
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Look at nature and meet nerds

claims.claim_text: A desktop machine still shipping with both a serial and a parallel port was already remarkable enough to comment on, marking how far these interfaces had receded from standard hardware.
claims.quote_verbatim: it came with not only a serial port, believe it or not, but a parallel port
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The parallel port gave direct access to pin states while a serial port needs a controller to interpret framed commands, and the parallel interface has become the harder of the two to find on modern hardware.
claims.quote_verbatim: Parallel port. Good luck finding one of those these days
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

The swapped-pins confession is the interviewer's own board and is attributed to Chris Gammell by content.
